question.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-3,2,6)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $r\cdot ⟨-2,4,4⟩=8.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a point on the plane. If $r=⟨x,y,z⟩,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-2,4,4⟩ & =8 \\ -2x+4y+4z & =8 \\ 4z & =8+2x-4y \\ z & =2+\frac{x}{2}-y.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $x=2$ and $y=1,$ we get 

$$
z=2+\frac{2}{2}-1=2.
$$

So, the point $Q(2,1,2)$ lies on the plane. 

Now, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,1,2⟩-⟨-3,2,6⟩ \\  & =⟨5,-1,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨-2,4,4⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|5\cdot (-2)+(-1)\cdot 4+(-4)\cdot 4|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{4}^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-10-4-16|}{\sqrt{4+16+16}} \\  & =\frac{|-30|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{30}{6} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
